title: AI labour governance in Asia is being negotiated as a South-South employment, skills, and digital-inclusion project rather than only a firm technology decision
source_unit: ILO report on Regional Policy Dialogue 2026: Harnessing AI to Build Employment-Friendly Labour Markets in ASEAN and China, published September 8, 2026
geography: ASEAN and China; regional policy dialogue held in Bangkok, Thailand, August 26-27, 2026

observations.period: August 26-27, 2026; ASEAN-China regional AI labour-policy dialogue

denominator.unit: regional policy dialogue involving governments, workers, and employers from ASEAN and China

policy_scope.value: Participants discussed AI transformation of labour markets, public employment services, skills-development systems, ethical and safe adoption, and employment-friendly policy

governance_principle.value: Human judgment and social dialogue were identified as essential to inclusive and resilient labour markets in the AI era

regional_route.value: South-South knowledge sharing was used to exchange policy innovations and practical pathways for AI governance

observations.method: Official ILO report of a regional policy dialogue and its stated takeaways; it is not a survey, firm-level evaluation, or causal assessment of AI policy.
observations.uncertainty: The dialogue records policy positions and knowledge exchange, not implementation, worker outcomes, AI productivity, job displacement, or the degree of consensus among participants.
observations.subgroup: Governments, worker and employer organizations, public employment services, skills systems, workers exposed to AI, and people affected by digital-access gaps across ASEAN and China.
observations.counterinterpretation: Dialogue can produce principles without changing firm incentives or state practice; “human judgment” may preserve discretion without guaranteeing worker control, fairness, or accountable remedies.

observations.period: 2026; AI exposure and uneven labour-market impact in South-East Asia

denominator.unit: workers in South-East Asia employed in jobs with potential generative-AI exposure

exposure.value: Almost 80 million workers in South-East Asia are employed in jobs with potential exposure to generative AI

unevenness.value: Participants emphasized that AI impacts will not be experienced equally and that digital divides must be included in governance

response.value: Reskilling and upskilling, public employment-service innovation, and attention to digital access were identified as response areas

observations.method: ILO regional dialogue citing an exposure estimate and discussing policy implications; the source does not provide country-by-country exposure distributions, task-level causal effects, or transition outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: Potential exposure is not job loss, task automation, productivity gain, or realized worker harm; the estimate's coverage and definition are not fully detailed in the news report.
observations.subgroup: Workers in South-East Asia with different occupations, skills, gender, income, sector, firm size, connectivity, and access to training or public employment services.
observations.counterinterpretation: Exposure may create complementarity and better work rather than displacement; digital divides can sometimes be narrowed through low-cost tools, but access alone does not ensure skills, bargaining power, or benefit capture.

observations.period: 2026; China-ASEAN South-South cooperation and standards coordination

coordination.value: China and ASEAN participants discussed alignment and coordination of development strategies, governance frameworks, and technical standards for AI

institutional_partners.value: The dialogue brought governments, workers' organizations, and employers' organizations into a shared AI-and-employment policy space

geopolitical_mechanism.value: South-South cooperation is positioned as a way to shape regional AI governance and translate technological opportunity into inclusive labour outcomes

observations.method: ILO report of a China-supported ASEAN regional cooperation project and policy dialogue; it does not establish binding standards, implementation, or geopolitical convergence.
observations.uncertainty: The report does not specify which standards will be adopted, how interests will be reconciled, or how regional coordination will affect national regulation, firms, or workers.
observations.subgroup: ASEAN and Chinese governments, regional labour institutions, worker and employer organizations, standards bodies, technology firms, and workers crossing regional value chains.
observations.counterinterpretation: South-South coordination can broaden policy agency, but it can also export dominant standards, leave smaller economies with limited leverage, or prioritize technology diffusion over rights and remedy.

related_sources.claim: ILO project page for the South-South employment cooperation project referenced in the report.

boundary: This record captures the policy-dialogue and regional-cooperation framing of AI labour governance in ASEAN and China. It does not establish AI job loss, productivity, worker outcomes, adopted standards, implementation, or causal effects of social dialogue.
